justifications.functional_suitability: R-01 through R-04 are comprehensively addressed. Video Mediation Service handles consultations, E-Prescription Integrator manages prescription transmissions, AI Orchestrator & Audit Logger with Model Execution Engine executes symptom triage, and Session & Consent Manager with Consent & Profile enforces granular patient consent.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Efficient performance is achieved via Global HTTPS Load Balancer, in-memory caching in Memorystore for Redis, asynchronous event streaming with Google Cloud Pub/Sub, and local caching via Offline Cache Manager to optimize responsiveness and minimize load on the Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability requirements are directly fulfilled. The Gateway Adapter Client and Prescription Transformation Engine within E-Prescription Integrator explicitly connect to Local Pharmacies and EU National E-Prescription Networks using HL7 FHIR and national REST/SOAP standards over HTTPS and mTLS.
justifications.usability: Web Application & Mobile Apps serves Patients and Licensed Clinicians across devices with Adaptive Video Streaming and Triage & AI Interface. However, explicit interfaces or portals for Platform Administrators and Pharmacy/Compliance Auditors identified in L2 are not detailed at the component level.
justifications.reliability: R-06 is handled by Adaptive Video Streaming with audio-only fallback and Bandwidth Adaptation Engine. Network disruptions are mitigated using Offline Cache Manager (SQLite/IndexedDB), while Resilience & Queue Manager and Idempotent Sync Coordinator ensure reliable recovery and message delivery.
justifications.security: Compliance with GDPR and HIPAA is enforced via regional isolation in Regional API Gateways, GCP Cloud Armor, and EU Pub/Sub Instance vs US Pub/Sub Instance. R-07 traceability is guaranteed by Audit Logger Interceptor and Immutable Ledger Writer into AI Audit Log Schema.
justifications.maintainability: High modularity is achieved through clear separation of concerns across services like Core Telehealth Service, Video Mediation Service, and E-Prescription Integrator. Components like Integration Anti-Corruption Layer and Prescription Transformation Engine decouple external systems, keeping coupling low and services independently maintainable.
justifications.portability: Cross-platform clients are supported using Flutter / React. Regional requirements on GCP (europe-west3 and us-central1) are honored. However, tight coupling to proprietary GCP services like Google Cloud Armor, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, and Memorystore for Redis reduces portability to alternate cloud environments.

PERF-01.justification: Signaling is offloaded to Go and Redis, while heavy WebRTC media streaming is handled externally by the Third-Party Video Provider, preventing backend bottlenecks during peak EU loads.
sensitivity_points: Redis session cache latency during concurrent signaling bursts
Capacity and connection limits of the external WebRTC provider
tradeoffs: Offloading media to a third-party provider reduces infrastructure load but increases external dependency

PERF-02.justification: Handling ~14 requests per second is well within capacity. The localized Model Execution Engine using ONNX/PyTorch evaluates models in-process and writes audit logs asynchronously via Pub/Sub.
sensitivity_points: Execution latency of ONNX/PyTorch models under concurrent worker loads
Asynchronous audit logging throughput to Pub/Sub
tradeoffs: Local model execution ensures sub-3s response times but requires more regional compute memory

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture incorporates an Adaptive Video Streaming client, a Bandwidth Adaptation Engine, and a Media Quality Policy Enforcer for audio fallback, alongside an Offline Cache Manager for notes.
sensitivity_points: Real-time packet loss and bandwidth threshold detection
Client-side SQLite sync reconciliation once connectivity stabilizes
tradeoffs: Dropping video to prioritize audio maintains continuity but degrades visual diagnostic capability

AVAIL-02.justification: Only us-central1 is specified for the US. If the entire US region fails, no secondary US region or automated regional DR topology exists to restore services without moving data to europe-west3.
sensitivity_points: Single US region dependency violating residency upon cross-region failover
Time required to provision fresh infrastructure in an alternate US region
tradeoffs: Restricting US data to a single GCP region prevents cross-border leakage but hampers disaster recovery

MOD-01.justification: Modifications are restricted to the Gateway Adapter Client and Prescription Transformation Engine within the E-Prescription Integrator container, completely isolating national integration variances from the core system.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between translation schemas and country-specific network protocols
tradeoffs: Abstracting national e-prescription adapters adds transformation overhead but protects core domain logic

MOD-02.justification: Models are sourced from the AI Symptom Checker Model Registry, while the Audit Logger Interceptor and Immutable Ledger Writer guarantee model versions and inputs are permanently linked in audit logs.
sensitivity_points: Model version tagging consistency across the registry and runtime engine
Immutability of logs for EU MDR regulatory compliance
tradeoffs: Synchronous audit interception ensures MDR compliance traceability at the expense of slight invocation latency

SEC-01.justification: The Session & Consent Manager contains an explicit Consent Evaluation Engine and accesses the Consent Ledger Schema to reject unauthorized cross-region data access before queries can execute.
sensitivity_points: Strictness and latency of the Consent Evaluation Engine rules
Accuracy of regional residency metadata on patient records
tradeoffs: Enforcing synchronous consent verification on every access attempt guarantees compliance but increases request latency

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates are captured by the Consent & Profile component and stored in the Consent Ledger Schema. Event Dispatcher broadcasts changes across Pub/Sub, though dedicated downstream research data redaction pipelines are unspecified.
sensitivity_points: Reliable end-to-end event propagation of consent revocations via Pub/Sub
Latency between consent ledger commit and downstream dataset exclusion
tradeoffs: Asynchronous event-based revocation decoupling scales well but risks temporary inconsistency before total propagation
